text: A ROS node that carries out long-running tasks on request and reports feedback and a result.
A collision object that has been fixed to a robot link in the planning scene, so it moves with the tool and is checked for collisions as part of the robot.
The Nav2 server that runs the behavior tree and calls the planner, controller and behavior servers.
The computer that runs the robot's program and decides what to do next, from a small microcontroller like an Arduino to an industrial robot controller.
The list in an ament_python package's setup.py that tells the build which extra files, such as launch and YAML files, to copy into the install space.
A Universal Robots add-on that, when its node runs in a pendant program, fetches a URScript program from the ROS driver on the PC and runs it so ROS can command the arm.
A 3D robot simulator with physics that simulates a robot, its sensors and its surroundings, and connects to ROS 2 so code can be tested before running on real hardware.
A color representation separating image data into hue (color type), saturation (color purity), and value (brightness) channels.
The component of a PID controller that integrates past tracking errors over time, eliminating residual steady-state droop.
KUKA Robot Language, the proprietary, Pascal-like programming language used to program KUKA industrial manipulators.
A robot that moves through its environment instead of staying bolted in place, such as a warehouse robot or planetary rover, and relies on sensors to map, localize and plan paths.
A MoveIt 2 library (MTC) that breaks a manipulation job such as pick and place into a chain of stages that are planned together and can be inspected one by one in RViz.
The Nav2 action a client uses to ask the robot to drive to a pose.
A RAPID function that returns a copy of a robtarget moved by given X, Y and Z distances in millimeters, in the work object's coordinate system.
An exchange of latched request and acknowledge signals (such as cycle-start, busy and done) between a PLC and a robot so each knows the other's state.
The component of a PID controller generating output directly proportional to the current instantaneous tracking error.
A named block of ABB RAPID code, from MODULE to ENDMODULE, that holds data declarations at the top followed by routines such as PROC, FUNC and TRAP.
An ABB RAPID function that shifts a target along the axes of the tool, often used to compute approach and retract points from a grip point.
An ABB RAPID data type that defines a complete robot position in millimeters, tool orientation as a quaternion, arm axis configurations, and external axis positions.
A device that measures the robot or its surroundings, such as an encoder, an ultrasonic range finder or a camera; it is the "sense" part of the sense, think, act loop.
A DC circuit configuration providing a path to supply common (-).
A DC circuit configuration providing a path to supply source (+).

Consistent odometry errors caused by physical robot imperfections, such as unequal wheel diameters or wheelbase uncertainty, that repeat identically across runs and can be corrected by software calibration.
A message_filters synchronization utility that aligns multiple incoming ROS 2 topic streams by matching their header timestamps.
A named, unidirectional communication channel in ROS over which nodes publish and subscribe to continuous data streams.
Unified Robot Description Format: an XML file that describes a robot as a tree of links joined by joints, with each joint's type, axis, position and limits.
A coordinate frame attached to a fixture or workpiece that program targets are measured from, so re-teaching it moves all targets without changing the program.
How to choose and size grippers, mount them and set payload, and program the digital I/O that opens a gripper, confirms a grip and talks to a PLC, in URScript and RAPID.

How robots turn a target into smooth setpoints: trapezoidal, triangular and S-curve profiles, cubic and quintic time scaling, joint, linear and circular interpolation, zones, and time parameterization in MoveIt.

3D perception for robotics: direct sensing versus 2D inference, stereo disparity geometry, point cloud filtering with PCL (PassThrough, VoxelGrid, outliers), RANSAC planes, Euclidean clustering, and bin picking.
Capstone project: build a pick-and-place task for a simulated UR5e with ROS 2, MoveIt 2 and the MoveIt Task Constructor on mock hardware or Gazebo, with milestones, tests and a rubric.
